title: Laughing at the barriers
lead: A little humor about everyday life with a disability. The joke is always on the barrier, never on the person.

slides.alt: A man in a wheelchair looks up a flight of stairs at a front door. A sign on the wall says the accessible entrance is around back.
slides.joke: “Accessible entrance around back.” Past the dumpsters, through the kitchen, left at the walk-in freezer. I didn't ask for a ramp. I asked to get in.

slides.alt: A blind woman with a white cane stands calmly while a man leans in and talks to her very loudly.
slides.joke: He keeps talking louder and slower. I'm blind, not far away.

slides.alt: Two Deaf friends sign to each other through a restaurant window, smiling.
slides.joke: Two Deaf friends can chat through a closed window or across a packed restaurant. Hearing people call that a superpower. We call it Tuesday.

slides.alt: A car with no placard sits in an accessible parking space while its driver chats on his phone. A woman in a wheelchair waits nearby.
slides.joke: Nobody is faster than the guy who parks in the accessible spot because he'll “just be a minute.” Twenty minutes later, he's still just a minute.

slides.alt: A man with a prosthetic leg walks through an airport security arch while an officer watches.
slides.joke: Airport security asked if I had anything to declare. Just my leg. It's carry-on.

slides.alt: An older woman with a walker reads a store sign pointing up a staircase to the only restroom.
slides.joke: The only restroom is upstairs, at the back, past the patio furniture. That's not a floor plan. That's a fitness test.

slides.alt: A stranger grabs the handles of a woman's wheelchair and starts pushing without asking. She looks back, unimpressed.
slides.joke: Please don't push my chair without asking. You wouldn't grab someone's legs to help them walk faster.

slides.alt: A man stands with his service dog, which wears a work vest. A passerby reaches out to pet the dog.
slides.joke: Yes, he's a very good boy. He's also at work. Pet him and you're filling out his timesheet.

slides.alt: A driver with a hearing aid leans toward a crackling drive-thru speaker.
slides.joke: Between my hearing aids and the drive-thru speaker, one of us is broken. It's not me.

slides.alt: A man in a wheelchair sits beside a calendar full of crossed-out days and a box marked part ships in six weeks.
slides.joke: My chair needed one small part. Six weeks. I could have grown it myself.

link.text: Why the right to repair matters

slides.alt: Four friends, one using a wheelchair, one a walker, one forearm crutches and one a white cane, stand in front of an elevator with an out of order sign.
slides.joke: Four different disabilities. One thing in common: the elevator is out of order. Again.
